1.title: From Champagne-Method Tradition to Independent AOC
1.html:
In the early 20th century, several Alsace estates were already making sparkling wine by the Champagne method (méthode champenoise). The tradition declined in the first half of the century around the Second World War, until the decree of 24 August 1976 officially recognised AOC Crémant d'Alsace, giving Alsace producers a framework for quality sparkling wine production with rules close to those of their Champagne counterparts.

Today more than 500 producers belong to the "Syndicat des Producteurs de Crémant d'Alsace".
2.title: Strict Whole-Bunch Pressing Rules
2.html:
• Whole-bunch pressing (vendange entière) is mandatory — grapes must go into the press as whole bunches, without being crushed first (foulage). This differs from still wines, where grapes may be crushed first to release juice, and is meant to protect the purity and delicacy of the juice to the greatest extent
  • Hand harvesting: using containers of less than 100 kg capacity, with the bunches delivered intact and whole to the press
  • Pressing ratio: only 100 litres of juice may be extracted from every 150 kg of grapes, a ratio far below ordinary winemaking; the "second/rebêche" last-pressing juice must be separated and must make up at least 2% of the declarable yield
  • Equipment rules: press equipment may not use Archimedes screws or chain mechanisms, to avoid excessive damage to the structure of the fruit
  • Earlier harvest dates: the harvest dates for Crémant are set by the "Alsace wine expert committee", usually opening a few days earlier than for still wines
3.title: Secondary Fermentation in Bottle and Ageing Rules
3.html:
Crémant d'Alsace must be made within Alsace by secondary fermentation in the bottle, with bottling (tirage) no earlier than 1 January of the year after harvest. Ageing on the lees may not be less than 9 months.

On yield limits, the 2007 rule set a base yield of 80 hl/ha, with the PLC flexible limit allowing a further 2.5%; grapes must reach a minimum natural alcohol of 8.5°. All Crémant d'Alsace wines must pass the statutory dual approval of analysis and sensory tasting.
4.question: What unique and mandatory rule applies to how grapes are pressed for Crémant d'Alsace?
4.options.0: Grapes must be crushed before pressing
4.options.1: Whole-bunch pressing (vendange entière) is mandatory: grapes must go into the press as whole bunches without being crushed first
4.options.2: There is no special rule; it is the same as for still wines
4.options.3: Only Archimedes screw presses may be used
4.explanation: The Crémant d'Alsace regulations mandate "whole-bunch pressing" (vendange entière): grapes must go into the press as whole bunches, without being crushed beforehand (foulage). This rule protects the purity and delicacy of the juice to the greatest extent and is one of the most distinctive technical features of the Crémant d'Alsace production rules; the regulations also expressly forbid Archimedes screw or chain-type press equipment.
5.keyPoints.0: The decree of 24 August 1976 officially recognised AOC Crémant d'Alsace; today more than 500 producers belong to the syndicate
5.keyPoints.1: Whole-bunch pressing (vendange entière) is mandatory, with no prior crushing and no Archimedes screw press equipment
5.keyPoints.2: Only 100 L of juice from every 150 kg of grapes, with the last-pressing juice separated and making up at least 2%
5.keyPoints.3: Secondary fermentation in bottle must be completed within Alsace, with at least 9 months on the lees
